fields.meta_title: Free Expense Report Form Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an expense report form that turns receipt photos into lines and sends each report to a manager. Reports save to a database you own.
fields.h1: Build an Expense Report Form That Checks Its Own Math
fields.hero_description: Describe your categories and who signs off. Emergent builds the expense report form, turns each receipt photo into a line and adds up the report. Every claim lands in one table.
fields.features_heading: Six Jobs a Spreadsheet Leaves to the Employee
fields.features_subheading: A template still needs someone to type every receipt and re-add the column. These pieces move that work into the form.
fields.feature_1:
Receipts read into line items

Photograph a receipt, and its merchant and amount fill the next line. Any field the app reads with low confidence goes back to the employee to confirm before the report sends.
fields.feature_2:
Categories that match your ledger

Offer the categories your bookkeeper already posts to, such as meals or software. Each line carries one, and the report subtotals every category before anyone signs off on it.
fields.feature_3:
Spending caps checked per line

Set a cap for any category, like a meal limit per guest. A line over its cap asks for a written reason before the report submits, and the approver reads it beside the amount.
fields.feature_4:
Cash advances netted against spend

Record the advance an employee drew before the job began. The report subtracts it from the spend and shows whether the company owes money or the employee owes some back.
fields.feature_5:
An approver for every report

Route each submitted report to the right manager for a decision. Approve it or send it back with a comment, and the decision is saved on the row with its time and approver.
fields.feature_6:
The whole app in your GitHub

Export the codebase to your GitHub repository when finance wants the expense app on its own servers or tied to an internal tool. The reports table comes along with the form.
fields.why_title: Why Build Expense Report Forms With Emergent?
fields.why_description: An Excel template holds the numbers but not the receipts. Nobody checks the totals until finance opens the file.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Teams Report What They Spend
fields.tab_content_1:
A day of receipts filed from the parking lot

After a day of client visits, a Northwind Supply rep photographs three receipts in her car. The form reads each into a line: an $86.40 client lunch, $24.00 for parking and $139.60 in sample kits. The parking stub is faded, and the app asks her to confirm it. Her $250.00 report reaches her manager before she pulls out.
fields.tab_content_2:
Grant codes checked on each line

Lakeview Youth Arts runs its programs on two grants. Program staff pick a grant code on each line of the expense report form, and a line without one blocks the submit button. Maya's $456.50 report splits across both: $312.00 of mural paint to the Arts Grant and $144.50 of printing to the Youth Fund.
fields.tab_content_3:
Meals over $75 a person need a reason

Brightline Agency caps client meals at $75 a person. An account director logs a $340 client dinner for four on her monthly report, and the line asks why. She types the pitch it was for. The report posts to #expense-approvals in Slack, where her manager approves the $1,128.90 total.
fields.tab_content_4:
Advances settled when the job wraps

Foremen at Acme Builders draw a $500 cash advance for small purchases on site. At the end of the job, the foreman logs $382.75 in hardware and fuel against it. The report subtracts the advance and shows $117.25 to return to the office. The approved report syncs to QuickBooks with its receipts attached.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Expense Report Form
fields.howto_description: Start from the policy your finance team already enforces, then turn each rule into a field or a check.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pull up the expense policy your team follows, or the email where finance last explained it. Note the categories, the cap on each and who signs off. Every rule in that document becomes a field or a check on the form.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Copy the expense accounts from your chart of accounts into a short dropdown list. Use the names your bookkeeper sees in the ledger, and each line lands in the right account without anyone recoding it at month end.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pick the amount above which a receipt photo is required, and whether lodging always needs one. A lower threshold means more uploads, while a higher one means more lines finance takes on trust. Write the number down first.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write one prompt in plain English that covers each rule from your notes, plus the approver. Emergent builds the expense report form, the reports table behind it and the approval step. Change any rule later by asking for it.
fields.howto_step_5_des: If employees draw cash advances, ask for an advance field that nets against spend. Teams that bill clients or report to funders can add a client or grant code to every line, picked from a dropdown instead of typed freehand.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Connect the approver and the books
fields.howto_step_6_des: Post each submitted report where the approver already works, such as a Slack channel or an inbox. Once a report is approved, push it to your accounting tool, such as QuickBooks or Xero, through its API.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Run last month's receipts through the form yourself, including one crumpled receipt and one line over a cap. Check the total against your own math, then open the new row in the reports table and confirm each field.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is downloadable grids (Template.net, Pinterest boards, WordLayouts, Harvest's nonprofit sheet) plus three form builders' reimbursement templates (Fillout, Jotform, Wufoo) and a Google Form template. The grids leave receipts in a separate folder and the math to the filer; the builder templates stop at collecting fields. This page answers what an expense report form holds and how to make one, then shows four teams whose form reads receipt photos, enforces a policy cap, codes spend to a grant and nets a cash advance. Travel and mileage claims stay on their sibling pages.
